title: History
tagline: Historians, chroniclers and the founding documents, from Herodotus to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
hero_caption: Bayeux Tapestry, scene 57: the death of King Harold at Hastings, embroidered c. 1070s (Bayeux Museum)
intro: Two intertwined canons: the books in which Western writers tried to record and explain the past, and the charters, declarations and constitutions that themselves changed its course. It runs from Herodotus and Thucydides through the medieval chroniclers, the humanists and the Enlightenment to the professional historians of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, alongside documents from Magna Carta to the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Manuscripts, original documents and early editions are shown from Wikimedia Commons; recent books still under copyright are described without images.
